question: The Padma Shri awardee Guru K Kalyanasundaram Pillai, the man who is keeping an ancient tradition alive,was awarded the Padma Shri 2023 for his contribution to the field of ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru K. Kalyanasundaram Pillai was conferred the Padma Shri 2023 (in the Art category) for his lifelong contribution to Bharatanatyam. (भरतनाट्यम)

• He belongs to the famous Thanjavur (Tanjore) hereditary lineage of dance masters and has headed the Sri Rajarajeshwari Bharata Natya Kala Mandir, Mumbai, one of the oldest Bharatanatyam institutions in India, teaching the traditional Thanjavur bani (style) for decades.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, derived from the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni and from the temple tradition of the *devadasis*. Its repertoire (*margam*) includes Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam, Tillana.

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India, after the Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan. The Padma awards are announced on Republic Day (26 January).

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Who appoints the State Election Commissioner?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Governor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor of the state. (राज्यपाल)

• This is provided under Article 243K (for Panchayats) and Article 243ZA (for Municipalities), inserted by the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, 1992.

• The State Election Commission superintends, directs and controls the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections to the Panchayats and Municipalities (local bodies).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The State Election Commissioner cannot be removed except in the manner and on the grounds prescribed for the removal of a Judge of a High Court, and his service conditions cannot be varied to his disadvantage after appointment — this protects his independence.

• Elections to Parliament and State Legislatures are conducted by the Election Commission of India (Article 324), whose members are appointed by the President.

NOTE

• Other appointments made by the Governor: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers, Advocate General (Article 165), Chairman and members of the State Public Service Commission (Article 316), Vice-Chancellors of state universities (as Chancellor).

question: In which river has the National Waterways-2 (NW-2) been developed in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmaputra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National Waterway-2 (NW-2) has been developed on the Brahmaputra river, on the Sadiya–Dhubri stretch in Assam, covering about 891 km. (ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी)

• It was declared a National Waterway in 1988 and is a key route for cargo movement to the North-East.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• NW-1 – the Ganga–Bhagirathi–Hooghly river system, Prayagraj to Haldia (1,620 km) — the longest National Waterway; the Jal Marg Vikas Project is being implemented on it.

• NW-3 – the West Coast Canal with the Champakara and Udyogmandal canals in Kerala (205 km) — India's first waterway with 24-hour navigation facilities.

• NW-4 – Godavari–Krishna rivers with the Kakinada–Puducherry canals; NW-5 – Brahmani–Mahanadi delta with the East Coast Canal.

NOTE

• Inland waterways are managed by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), set up in 1986, under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. The National Waterways Act, 2016 declared 111 waterways as National Waterways.

question: In India, Micro Finance Institutions primarily target which segment of the population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Low-income individuals and small businesses.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs) provide small-value loans and other financial services without collateral to low-income households, poor individuals and very small businesses that are not served by mainstream banks. (सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थान — निम्न आय वर्ग)

• Their aim is financial inclusion — bringing the unbanked poor, especially rural women and micro-entrepreneurs, into the formal credit system.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Microfinance in India is delivered mainly through the Self Help Group–Bank Linkage Programme (SHG-BLP) launched by NABARD in 1992, and through NBFC-MFIs regulated by the RBI.

• Bandhan Bank and Ujjivan grew out of microfinance operations. MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency), 2015, refinances micro-enterprise lending under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun categories).

NOTE

• The modern microfinance movement is associated with Prof. Muhammad Yunus and the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh, who jointly received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.

question: What is the name of the scheme launched by Himachal Pradesh government for dairy farmers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanjeevani.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Himachal Pradesh government launched "Project Sanjeevani" (April 2023) to empower dairy farmers of the state. (परियोजना संजीवनी — हिमाचल प्रदेश)

• The project aims to strengthen the dairy value chain — improving animal health care and veterinary services, breed improvement, fodder and nutrition support, and better milk collection and marketing — so that dairying becomes a reliable source of rural income.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Dairying is a major allied activity supporting farmers' incomes in the hill state of Himachal Pradesh, where land holdings are small and fragmented.

• At the national level, dairy development is supported by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), Anand (Gujarat), and schemes such as the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) and the Rashtriya Gokul Mission (for indigenous breeds).

NOTE

• India is the world's largest producer of milk. Operation Flood (the "White Revolution"), launched in 1970 under Dr. Verghese Kurien, made India self-sufficient in milk; Kurien is called the "Father of the White Revolution".

question: Which of the following States will host the 37th National Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 37th National Games were hosted by Goa, from 25 October to 9 November 2023. (गोवा)

• The mascot of the Games was "Moga", the Indian Gaur (bison), which is the state animal of Goa; the main venue was the Shri Shiv Chhatrapati / Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, Fatorda and other venues across the state.

• Maharashtra topped the medal tally at the 37th National Games.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The 36th National Games (2022) were held in Gujarat, where Services Sports Control Board topped the medal tally.

• The National Games are India's premier multi-sport domestic event, organised under the aegis of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA). The first edition was held in 1924 at Lahore (as the All India Olympic Games).

NOTE

• The 38th National Games (2025) were hosted by Uttarakhand. Goa's National Games were notable for including beach sports, given its long coastline.

question: Kalidas Samman is a prestigious arts award presented annually by the government of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kalidas Samman is a prestigious arts award instituted in 1980 and presented annually by the Government of Madhya Pradesh. (कालिदास सम्मान — मध्य प्रदेश)

• It is given in four fields by rotation — Classical Music, Classical Dance, Theatre and Plastic Arts (visual arts).

• It is named after Kalidasa, the great Sanskrit poet and dramatist, author of Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghadutam, Raghuvamsam and Kumarasambhavam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Notable recipients include Pt. Ravi Shankar, Pt. Bhimsen Joshi, Ustad Bismillah Khan, M. F. Husain, Birju Maharaj and Ebrahim Alkazi.

• Madhya Pradesh also confers the Tansen Samman (Hindustani classical music), the Lata Mangeshkar Award (light/film music) and the Maharishi Ved Vyas Samman.

NOTE

• Ujjain in Madhya Pradesh is associated with Kalidasa; the state also organises the annual Kalidasa Samaroh at Ujjain, a festival of Sanskrit drama and the arts.

question: How many countries will participate in ICC 2023 ODI Cricket World Cup?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 (ODI World Cup) was played by 10 teams, in a single round-robin format followed by semi-finals and the final. (10 टीमें)

• It was hosted entirely by India (5 October – 19 November 2023), the first time India hosted the tournament alone.

• The ten teams: India, Australia, England, Pakistan, New Zealand, South Africa, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Sri Lanka and the Netherlands.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Australia won the 2023 title (their 6th), beating India in the final at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad.

• Virat Kohli was adjudged Player of the Tournament and scored a record 765 runs; Mohammed Shami took 24 wickets.

• The mascots were "Tonk" and "Blaze".

NOTE

• ODI World Cup winners: West Indies (1975, 1979), India (1983, 2011), Australia (1987, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2015, 2023), Pakistan (1992), Sri Lanka (1996), England (2019).

question: Whose autobiography is titled ‘Born Again on the Mountain: a story of losing everything and finding it back’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arunima Sinha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Born Again on the Mountain: A Story of Losing Everything and Finding It Back" is the autobiography of Arunima Sinha, the world's first female amputee to climb Mount Everest (2013). (अरुणिमा सिन्हा)

• A former national-level volleyball player, she lost her left leg after being thrown from a moving train by robbers in 2011; she went on to summit Everest with a prosthetic leg and later climbed the highest peaks of several continents.

• She has been honoured with the Padma Shri (2015) and the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bachendri Pal – the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest (23 May 1984); her book is "Everest: My Journey to the Top".

• Santosh Yadav – the first woman in the world to climb Everest twice (1992 and 1993).

• Dicky Dolma – of Himachal Pradesh, one of the youngest women to scale Everest (1993, at 19).

NOTE

• Mount Everest (8,848.86 m), in the Himalayas on the Nepal–Tibet border, is called Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet. It was first climbed by Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary on 29 May 1953.

question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of money?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Perishability.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Perishability" (the tendency to decay or spoil quickly) is NOT a characteristic of good money. Money must last, not perish. (नाशवानता — मुद्रा का गुण नहीं)

• The essential qualities of good money are:

◦ Durability – it should not wear out or decay quickly.

◦ Portability – it should be easy to carry.

◦ Divisibility – it should be divisible into smaller units (rupees into paise) without loss of value.

◦ Homogeneity/Uniformity, Stability of value, General acceptability, Cognisability (easy to recognise) and Limited supply/scarcity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The functions of money are classified as:

◦ Primary – a medium of exchange and a measure/unit of value.

◦ Secondary – a store of value, a standard of deferred payments and a means of transfer of value.

• Money removes the problems of barter, chiefly the "double coincidence of wants".

NOTE

• In India, currency notes (except the ₹1 note) are issued by the Reserve Bank of India under the Minimum Reserve System (since 1957); coins and the ₹1 note are issued by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

question: Among the given options, which one causes an echo?
option_2: When sound waves travel through a solid medium
option_3: When sound waves travel through a liquid medium
option_4: When sound waves travel through a vacuum
solution_text:
The correct answer is When sound is reflected.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An echo is produced by the reflection of sound from a hard, distant obstacle (a wall, a cliff, a large building). (प्रतिध्वनि — ध्वनि का परावर्तन)

• Conditions for hearing a distinct echo:

◦ The persistence of hearing in the human ear is about 0.1 second, so the reflected sound must reach the ear at least 0.1 s after the original sound.

◦ Taking the speed of sound in air as 344 m/s at 22°C, the minimum distance between the source and the reflector must be ≥ 17.2 m (since 344 × 0.1 ÷ 2 = 17.2).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 and 3 merely describe propagation of sound through media; sound in fact travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids and slowest in gases — but travelling through a medium does not by itself create an echo.

• Option 4 is impossible: sound cannot travel through a vacuum at all, because it is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium.

NOTE

• Applications of reflection of sound: SONAR (Sound Navigation and Ranging) for measuring ocean depth, ultrasonography, megaphones/soundboards and the whispering galleries (e.g., in the Gol Gumbaz, Bijapur). Multiple reflections produce reverberation.

question: ____________ has two traditions: one is the sankeertana (which is the devotional aspect) and the other is the raasa.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri dance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Manipuri dance, the classical dance of Manipur, has two main traditions — the Sankeertana (the devotional, ritual aspect, performed by men with the pung/dholak drum and cymbals) and the Raas Leela (raasa), which depicts the love of Radha and Krishna. (मणिपुरी नृत्य)

• Its movements are gentle, flowing and rounded, with no sharp jerks; the female dancers wear the distinctive stiff, barrel-shaped skirt called the kumil (potloi) and a translucent veil.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The dance was popularised in modern times by Rabindranath Tagore, who introduced it at Santiniketan. Famous exponents include the Jhaveri Sisters and Guru Bipin Singh.

• Sankirtana of Manipur was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013.

NOTE

• Other options: Odissi (Odisha – tribhanga posture), Sattriya (Assam – from the *sattras* founded by Srimanta Sankardeva) and Chhau (a semi-classical masked dance of Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal).

question: Which of the following lakes is a saltwater lake ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chilika.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chilika Lake, on the east coast of Odisha, is a brackish/saltwater lagoon — it is connected to the Bay of Bengal by a narrow channel, so sea water mixes with the fresh water brought by rivers such as the Daya. (चिल्का झील — खारे पानी की झील)

• It is the largest brackish-water lagoon in India and the largest coastal lagoon in Asia, spread over roughly 1,100 sq km in the rainy season.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lake Superior (North America) is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area, one of the five Great Lakes.

• Lake Malawi (also called Lake Nyasa) in the East African Rift is a freshwater lake, famous for its cichlid fishes.

• Lake Titicaca, on the Peru–Bolivia border, is a freshwater lake and the highest navigable lake in the world.

NOTE

• Chilika was the first Indian wetland designated a Ramsar Site (1981). It is famous for the Irrawaddy dolphins and for migratory birds, and contains the Nalabana Bird Sanctuary. Other saltwater lakes in India: Sambhar (Rajasthan) — the largest inland salt lake, Pulicat (Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu) and Lonar (Maharashtra).

question: ‘Wings of Fire’ is an autobiography of whom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is APJ Abdul Kalam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wings of Fire: An Autobiography" (1999) was written by Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam with Arun Tiwari. (विंग्स ऑफ फायर — ए. पी. जे. अब्दुल कलाम)

• It traces his life from a humble childhood in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu, to his work at ISRO and DRDO, where he led the SLV-III launch and the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Dr. Kalam served as the 11th President of India (2002–2007) and is called the "Missile Man of India" and the "People's President". He received the Bharat Ratna in 1997.

• His other books: India 2020: A Vision for the New Millennium, Ignited Minds, My Journey, Turning Points, Transcendence.

• His birthday, 15 October, is observed as World Students' Day.

NOTE

• Other autobiographies/memoirs: "An Indian Pilgrim" and "The Indian Struggle" (Subhas Chandra Bose), "My Truth" (Indira Gandhi), "The Story of My Experiments with Truth" (Mahatma Gandhi), "An Autobiography / Toward Freedom" (Jawaharlal Nehru).

question: The _______________ of the Indian Constitution defines the Fundamental Duties of Indian Citizens.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 51A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51A in Part IV-A of the Constitution lays down the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens. (अनुच्छेद 51A — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

• They were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, originally as ten duties.

• The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added the eleventh duty — that every parent/guardian shall provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between 6 and 14 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by the courts — and were borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

• They include duties to abide by the Constitution and respect the National Flag and National Anthem, cherish the ideals of the freedom struggle, protect the sovereignty of India, promote harmony, protect the environment, develop scientific temper, safeguard public property and strive towards excellence.

NOTE

• Article 21A (added by the 86th Amendment, 2002) provides for the Right to Education for children aged 6–14 years. "Article 41B" and "Article 49C" do not exist; Article 41 deals with the right to work/education/public assistance and Article 49 with the protection of monuments (both are Directive Principles).

question: Dr. Bhupendra Kumar Hazarika won the Bharat Ratna award in the field of ________ in 2019.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Music.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Bhupen Hazarika (Bhupendra Kumar Hazarika) was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2019 (posthumously) for his outstanding contribution to music. (भूपेन हजारिका — संगीत)

• Known as the "Bard of the Brahmaputra" and "Sudhakantha", he was a legendary singer, lyricist, composer and film-maker from Assam, whose songs (e.g., "Bistirno Parore", the Assamese version of "Ol' Man River", and "Dil Hoom Hoom Kare") celebrated humanism and communal harmony.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bhupen Hazarika received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1992), the Padma Shri (1977), the Padma Bhushan (2001) and the Padma Vibhushan (2012, posthumously). He also served as Chairman of the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

• In 2019, the Bharat Ratna was conferred on three persons: Bhupen Hazarika, Pranab Mukherjee (public affairs) and Nanaji Deshmukh (social work) — the latter two also posthumously in Nanaji's case.

NOTE

• The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award, instituted in 1954. It carries no monetary grant; the recipient gets a Sanad (certificate) signed by the President and a peepal-leaf-shaped medallion. The Dhola–Sadiya bridge over the Lohit river in Assam is named the Bhupen Hazarika Setu.

question: What type of vegetation is represented by Sundarbans, the world's largest delta located in the Bay of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mangrove Forests.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sundarbans, in the Ganga–Brahmaputra–Meghna delta (the world's largest delta) on the Bay of Bengal, is covered by Mangrove (littoral and swamp) forests. (मैंग्रोव / ज्वारीय वन)

• Mangroves grow in saline, waterlogged tidal areas and have special adaptations — stilt/prop roots and pneumatophores (breathing roots) that project above the mud to take in oxygen.

• The name "Sundarbans" is derived from the Sundari tree (Heritiera fomes), the dominant mangrove species there.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Sundarbans is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987), a Ramsar Site, a Biosphere Reserve (1989) and a Tiger Reserve, famous for the Royal Bengal Tiger and the estuarine crocodile.

• Other Indian mangrove areas: the Bhitarkanika (Odisha), Godavari–Krishna delta (Andhra Pradesh), Pichavaram (Tamil Nadu) and the Gulf of Kachchh (Gujarat).

NOTE

• Vegetation types in India: Tropical Evergreen, Tropical Deciduous (Monsoon), Tropical Thorn (in areas with less than 70 cm rainfall — Rajasthan, Gujarat), Montane (Himalayan) and Mangrove/Tidal forests.

question: The Mumbai High region in Arabian Sea is known for mining ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is mineral oil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mumbai High (Bombay High), an offshore field in the Arabian Sea about 160 km west of Mumbai, is India's largest producer of mineral oil (petroleum) and natural gas. (खनिज तेल)

• It was discovered in 1974 with the help of the Soviet exploration vessel Sagar Samrat, and production began in 1976. It is operated by the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other major oil fields in India: Digboi, Naharkatiya and Moran (Assam), Ankleshwar, Kalol and Khambhat (Gujarat), and the Krishna–Godavari (KG) basin offshore Andhra Pradesh.

• Digboi (Assam) is the oldest oil refinery/oilfield in India (oil struck in 1889).

NOTE

• India's uranium is mined chiefly at Jaduguda (Jharkhand) and Tummalapalle (Andhra Pradesh); coal comes mainly from Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh (Jharia, Raniganj, Korba, Talcher); copper from Khetri (Rajasthan), Singhbhum (Jharkhand) and Malanjkhand (Madhya Pradesh).

question: In which of the following years was the Child Marriage Restraint Act passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1929.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Child Marriage Restraint Act was passed in 1929 and came into force in 1930. (बाल विवाह निरोधक अधिनियम, 1929)

• It is popularly known as the "Sarda Act", after Rai Sahib Harbilas Sarda, the member of the Central Legislative Assembly who introduced the Bill.

• It originally fixed the minimum age of marriage at 14 years for girls and 18 years for boys; this was later raised to 18 and 21 respectively (by the 1978 amendment).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Act was repealed and replaced by the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, which provides for Child Marriage Prohibition Officers and makes such marriages voidable at the option of the child.

• Other social-reform legislations: Abolition of Sati (Regulation XVII of 1829) by Lord William Bentinck, the Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856 (efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar), and the Age of Consent Act, 1891 (Behramji Malabari).

NOTE

• The Act applied to all communities in British India. The reform movement against child marriage was strongly supported by leaders such as Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Keshab Chandra Sen and the Arya Samaj.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, identify the correct pair of State and Union Territories which recorded the highest literacy rate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala and Lakshadweep.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011:

◦ Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate among States — about 94.0%.

◦ Lakshadweep recorded the highest literacy rate among Union Territories — about 91.8%.

• India's overall literacy rate in 2011 was 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%). (साक्षरता दर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Lowest literacy: Bihar among the states (61.8%) and Dadra & Nagar Haveli among the UTs.

• Mizoram (91.3%) was second among the states and Goa third; Chandigarh and Puducherry followed Lakshadweep among the UTs.

• A person aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language is treated as literate.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th Census of India and the 7th after Independence. Its motto was "Our Census, Our Future". Other 2011 facts: population 121.09 crore, sex ratio 943, density 382 persons/sq km, most populous state Uttar Pradesh.

question: The sal tree assumes great significance in a number of tribal communities scattered across eastern India. For instance, ________ festival is celebrated in honour of the tree in Jharkhand.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarhul.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sarhul is the spring festival of the tribal communities of Jharkhand (Oraon, Munda, Ho, Santhal) celebrated in honour of the sal tree, when it bursts into flower. (सरहुल — साल वृक्ष की पूजा)

• "Sarhul" literally means "worship of the sal". The village priest (Pahan) offers sal flowers to the village deity Sarna Maa, and only after this ritual may people use the new flowers and fruits of the season.

• It is celebrated in the month of Chaitra (March–April) and marks the beginning of the new year for these communities.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Karma – celebrated in Bhadra (August–September) in honour of the Karam tree, for prosperity and good harvest.

• Sohrai – a harvest and cattle festival celebrated around Diwali, famous for Sohrai wall paintings (a GI-tagged art of Hazaribagh).

• Tusu Parab (Makar Parab) – a harvest festival of the Jharkhand–West Bengal–Odisha belt, celebrated at Makar Sankranti.

NOTE

• The Sal (Shorea robusta) is the state tree of Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, and is central to tribal life and the Sarna religious tradition.

question: Geto Sora won the Arena Junior (Boys) International Badminton Championship. He belongs to which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arunachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Geto Sora, the young shuttler who won the Arena Junior (Boys) International Badminton Championship, belongs to Arunachal Pradesh. (अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

• His success was widely celebrated as a landmark for badminton in the North-East, where sporting infrastructure has traditionally been limited.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Badminton is governed worldwide by the Badminton World Federation (BWF) and in India by the Badminton Association of India (BAI).

• India's leading badminton players include Pullela Gopichand, Saina Nehwal, P. V. Sindhu, Kidambi Srikanth, Lakshya Sen and the doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy–Chirag Shetty. India won the Thomas Cup in 2022 for the first time.

NOTE

• Key badminton terms: smash, drop shot, net shot, drive, lift, let, deuce, rally. A match is the best of three games of 21 points (rally-point scoring). The Arunachal Pradesh state animal is the Mithun and its capital is Itanagar.

question: Identify the Chhau dancer from the following, who received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award-2021 (given in February 2023)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhuvan Kumar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bhuvan Kumar received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for the year 2021 (formally presented in February 2023) for his contribution to Chhau dance. (छऊ नृत्य)

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Puraskar is India's highest national recognition conferred on practising artists of music, dance and drama. It carries a Tamrapatra (copper plaque), an angavastram, and a cash prize of ₹1,00,000.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chhau is a semi-classical dance with martial, tribal and folk elements, performed mainly during the Chaitra Parva spring festival. It has three recognised styles:

◦ Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand) – masked;

◦ Purulia Chhau (West Bengal) – masked, with large elaborate masks;

◦ Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha) – danced without masks.

• Chhau dance was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

• Kumkum Dhar is a well-known exponent of Kathak (Lucknow gharana).

NOTE

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance and Drama, was set up in 1952–53 and is headquartered in New Delhi. Its highest honour is the Akademi Ratna (Fellowship), limited to 40 living persons at a time.

question: Which of the following Indian musicians was referred to as ‘Ghazal King’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jagjit Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jagjit Singh (1941–2011) is popularly known as the "Ghazal King" (also the "Ghazal Maestro") of India. (ग़ज़ल सम्राट)

• Born in Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan, he made the ghazal accessible to ordinary listeners by simplifying its language and setting it to modern orchestration. His album "The Unforgettables" (1976), with his wife Chitra Singh, was a landmark.

• Famous ghazals: "Hothon Se Chhoo Lo Tum", "Tum Itna Jo Muskura Rahe Ho", "Woh Kagaz Ki Kashti", "Jhuki Jhuki Si Nazar".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2003. He composed music for the TV serial Mirza Ghalib (directed by Gulzar) and for films such as *Arth*, *Saath Saath* and *Prem Geet*.

• Ghulam Ali and Mehdi Hassan were celebrated Pakistani ghazal singers (Mehdi Hassan was called the "Shahenshah-e-Ghazal" — King of Kings of Ghazal); Pankaj Udhas was an Indian ghazal singer famous for "Chitthi Aayi Hai".

NOTE

• A ghazal is a poetic form of couplets (sher) sharing a common rhyme (radif/qafiya), of Persian–Urdu origin, usually on themes of love and loss. Great ghazal poets: Mirza Ghalib, Mir Taqi Mir, Faiz Ahmed Faiz, Firaq Gorakhpuri.

question: On 8th April 1929, who among the following two revolutionists threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly?
option_2: Bhagat Singh and Ram Prasad Bismil
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 8 April 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw two low-intensity bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly, Delhi, and shouted the slogan "Inquilab Zindabad", showering leaflets. (भगत सिंह और बटुकेश्वर दत्त)

• The bombs were deliberately thrown at an empty part of the chamber so as not to kill anyone — their aim, in their own words, was "to make the deaf hear". They did not run away but courted arrest.

• The protest was against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill, seen as measures to crush the workers' and revolutionary movements.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Both belonged to the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA), formed in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi, under Chandra Shekhar Azad.

• Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged on 23 March 1931 at Lahore in the Lahore Conspiracy Case for the killing of J. P. Saunders (December 1928, in revenge for the assault on Lala Lajpat Rai). 23 March is observed as Shaheed Diwas.

• Batukeshwar Dutt was sentenced to transportation for life and sent to the Cellular Jail, Andaman.

NOTE

• Bhagat Singh founded the Naujawan Bharat Sabha (1926) and wrote the famous essay "Why I am an Atheist". Ram Prasad Bismil was hanged in 1927 in the Kakori Conspiracy Case and so could not have been present in 1929.
